presets.name: Even clean guitar
presets.desc: Transparent 4:1 with a 6 dB knee and dual-path release: strums sit at one level, no pumping between them
presets.notes: The doc's clean-guitar row, golem's Standard

presets.name: Chicken-picking squash
presets.desc: OTA pedal squash, 8:1 with a 3 ms attack: snappy pick click on top, every note of a hybrid-picked run equal

refs.why: Nashville session lines played through a compressor pedal

presets.notes: The doc's funk / country row. Before the amp, into a clean Fender-type voice

presets.name: Squash with the pick kept
presets.desc: Same pedal squash blended 60 % with the dry: sustain from the wet, the natural pick attack from the dry
presets.notes: The doc's parallel row; the blend-knob pedals' trick. Coherent mix means no comb at 60 %

presets.name: Funk chop, compressed clean
presets.desc: FET 4:1, 8 ms attack, fast release, 80 % wet: tight 16th-note scratches that pop out evenly without losing snap

refs.why: bright, even, mostly direct funk rhythm guitar

presets.notes: Accounts of Rodgers' chain disagree on compression; this is the sound in its spirit, not a documented setting

presets.name: Singing lead sustain
presets.desc: Pedal-style compressor before a fuzz or drive: long notes hold and bloom, a hot front end for endless sustain

refs.why: Gilmour's compressor pedal into a fuzz for the solo's sustain
refs.source: Guitar World feature, reprinted in Australian Guitar, 2021

presets.notes: Long release so the gain rises slowly as the note decays: sustain without an audible swell

presets.name: Drop-tuned rhythm control
presets.desc: Clean 3:1 with a 150 Hz sidechain low cut: evens out low-tuned riffs without the low strings pumping the mix
presets.notes: After the amp and cab. High-gain is already compressed: this only catches the open-string peaks

presets.name: Acoustic strum leveller
presets.desc: Gentle opto 3:1 with an 80 Hz sidechain cut: a piezo or mic'd acoustic stays even, body thumps don't duck it
presets.notes: Slow-ish opto keeps the strum's attack; the sidechain cut stops a palm slap from pulling the whole level down

presets.name: Glue after amp and cab
presets.desc: Bus 2.5:1, 30 ms attack, 250 ms release: 2 – 3 dB of glue after the cab, transients kept

presets.name: Fingerstyle bass, smooth opto
presets.desc: Opto 4:1, slow attack, two-stage release: fingerstyle notes even out, warm and unobtrusive

refs.why: mixer Mick Guzauski picks a slow LA-2A for smooth vocals and bass
refs.source: Universal Audio blog, 10 Questions with Mick Guzauski (undated)

presets.notes: Opto's release lengthens after long reduction, so a held note never swells back up audibly

presets.name: Anchored rock bass
presets.desc: FET 6:1, 35 ms attack, 120 Hz sidechain low cut: pick attack through, sustain locked, the low E doesn't pump
presets.notes: golem's Bass anchor from the doc's bass row; drive 20 % adds the FET's odd harmonics for small-speaker audibility

presets.name: Slap and pop control
presets.desc: Fast feed-forward 8:1 with a 1 ms attack: thumb slaps and pops tamed so the ghost notes come up

refs.why: slap pioneer whose rack held a fast dbx 160X compressor

presets.notes: Clean = feed-forward like a VCA; the full-band detector is wanted here, pops are what must trigger it

presets.name: Smooth vocal leveller
presets.desc: Opto 3:1, 25 ms attack, two-stage release: a lead vocal levelled without audible grab, warm and forward

refs.why: mixer Carlos de la Garza starts every vocal on a Gray LA-2A
refs.source: Universal Audio blog, Carlos de la Garza interview (undated)

presets.notes: The doc's voice row, golem's Vocal opto; sidechain cut keeps plosives and stage rumble from pumping it

presets.name: Upfront rock vocal
presets.desc: FET 6:1, 2 ms attack, fast release with a little drive: a shouted vocal pinned in front of loud guitars
presets.notes: FET shortens its times further on short peaks: every syllable stays at the front in a dense mix

presets.name: Thick parallel vocal
presets.desc: FET squeezed 7 – 10 dB and blended about 30 % under the dry vocal: thickness and punch, the dynamics stay

refs.why: Chiccarelli tucked a heavily squeezed parallel 1176 under the lead vocal
refs.source: Vintage King, Five Sounds with Joe Chiccarelli, 2022

presets.notes: Slow-to-mid attack, fast-to-mid release as in the interview; mix 30 % stands for the parallel bus fader

presets.name: Drum bus glue
presets.desc: Bus 4:1, 30 ms attack, auto release: 2 – 4 dB on the kit, hits keep their crack, the kit sounds as one
presets.notes: Bus-console style settings; sidechain cut so the kick alone doesn't duck the cymbals

presets.name: Crushed parallel drums
presets.desc: FET 10:1 crushing the kit, blended 35 % with the dry: sustain and room come up, the transients stay dry
presets.notes: New York-style parallel compression in one block; the coherent mix means no comb when blending

presets.name: Keys glue
presets.desc: Bus 2:1, slow attack and release: keys and pads gently held together, playing dynamics intact

presets.name: Gentle leveller, capped
presets.desc: Clean 2:1 with a wide knee and reduction capped at 6 dB: evens any source, can never squash it
presets.notes: The doc's range row, golem's Gentle
